title: 2008 AMC 12A Problem 18
statement: Triangle \(ABC,\) with sides of length \(5,\) \(6,\) and \(7,\) has one vertex on the positive \(x\)-axis, one on the positive \(y\)-axis, and one on the positive \(z\)-axis. Let \(O\) be the origin. What is the volume of tetrahedron \(OABC?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(A = (a, 0, 0),\) \(B = (0, b, 0),\) \(C = (0, 0, c).\) Assigning the sides, \[ \begin{aligned} a^2 + b^2 &= 25, \\ b^2 + c^2 &= 36, \\ a^2 + c^2 &= 49. \end{aligned} \]

Adding gives \(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 = 55,\) so \(a^2 = 19,\) \(b^2 = 6,\) and \(c^2 = 30.\)

The volume is \[ \begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{6}abc &= \dfrac{1}{6}\sqrt{19 \cdot 6 \cdot 30} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{6}\sqrt{3420} \\ &= \sqrt{95}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Let the vertices be \((a, 0, 0),\) \((0, b, 0),\) \((0, 0, c)\) and write the three side-length equations
Adding the three equations gives \(a^2 + b^2 + c^2,\) and the volume is \(\tfrac{1}{6}abc\)
